collections.title: All 25th Stamped Cards
collections.description: The 25th-anniversary logos, from Celebrations and its Japanese counterparts to Happy Meals, cereal boxes, jumbo First Partners and the Creatures gift deck. Different finishes and oversized copies have their own places here.
collections.coverage: Includes the languages currently in the catalog. Other international languages, Korean and Traditional Chinese are not yet cataloged; this is not a worldwide completeness claim.

description.text: The English booster cards carry the Pikachu 25 logo. The two metal UPC replicas are omitted: they reproduce Base Set cards without that stamp; the gold Pikachu V and Poké Ball promos appear below.
Japan uses a blue-and-gold 25th graphic. Includes the main set, basic Energy, mirror-holo parallels and all 25 Promo Card Pack reprints.
The Golden Box deck has its own 25th graphic, including on its Trainers and Energy. The 30-card Creatures Corporate History deck has a gold anniversary stamp and unusual historical card backs.

The stamped product promos, including the UPC's gold Pikachu V and Poké Ball, Greninja ☆, Professor Burnet and the Pikachu V-UNION pieces. The assembled V-UNION design carries the anniversary branding; its four pieces are kept together in this checklist.

groups.title: Pikachu V-UNION Special Collection and Premium Playmat Collection

description.text: All 25 McDonald's cards, in both finishes, plus General Mills Pikachu SWSH039. Only Pikachu in the cereal promotion has the anniversary logo: the other five cereal holos are excluded even where provider data labels them as stamped.
The jumbo Pikachu from the collector's binder and the 24 jumbo starters from the eight First Partner Packs. These are oversized cards, not their original playing-size prints.

collections.title: All 30th Stamped Cards
collections.description: The 30th-anniversary mark across English, Japanese and Simplified Chinese cards, grouped by how you get them: booster packs, decks, the promos inside boxes and collections, the First Partner illustrations, and store and event giveaways. Includes the "What's your favorite?" retailer promos and the two Pokémon Day 2026 promos, whose stamps are built around the 30th emblem, and announced cards cataloged ahead of their release.
collections.coverage: Includes the languages currently in the catalog. Other international languages, Korean and Traditional Chinese are not yet cataloged; this is not a worldwide completeness claim.

description.text: Every card here comes out of 30th Celebration booster packs, in all three cataloged languages: the main set, Classic Collection reprints, secret rares and anniversary basic Energy.

Cards that come only with a deck: the Japanese Premium Deck Set and the Simplified Chinese Deluxe Deck Set, and the English Espeon ex and Umbreon ex Battle Decks. The Battle Decks hold stamped reverse holos of 30th Celebration cards, such as two of the Eevees, and of cards from other Mega Evolution and Scarlet & Violet sets, plus their Victini and Zeraora promos.

see.name: 30th Celebration Premium Deck Set Espeon & Umbreon

description.text: The promo each sealed product holds, which its packs never do: the English ex boxes and jumbos, sticker, poster and figure collections, Ditto, both Ultra-Premium Collections, Nidorina in both Elite Trainer Boxes, the Eevee foil from the 2-Pack Blister and Knock Out Collection, and the Pokémon Day 2026 Collection Pikachu, whose Pokémon Day stamp is built around the 30th anniversary emblem. Also the FUTURISTIC BOX Pikachu ex pair in Japanese and Simplified Chinese, and the Chinese display-box and card-display promos. Cards from ordinary packs bundled with these products do not qualify just because of the packaging.

groups.title: Collection Display Box Espeon ex & Umbreon ex

copies.note: Every copy of this promo prints the 30th anniversary mark, so the plain copy carries no stamp of its own in the data.
The Pokémon Center copy: its stamp is the Pokémon Center one, beside the card's 30th anniversary mark.

description.text: All 27 starters in each of the three cataloged languages, from the First Partner collections: English MEP 037–063, Japanese M-P 101–127 and Simplified Chinese 30th-P 001–027. They are product promos too, kept together here.

description.text: Handed out rather than sold in a box: the "What's your favorite?" promos, given with Pokémon TCG purchases at retailers, whose Pokémon 30 logo stands in for the anniversary mark (Pitch Black's Armarouge, Primarina and Zarude, 30th Celebration's Mewtwo, and Delta Reign's Kyogre, Giratina and Groudon); the Pokémon Day 2026 Bulbasaur from store events, its Pokémon Day stamp built around the 30th anniversary emblem; Japan's 30th CELEBRATION Promo Card Pack from Pokémon Card Gym battles and the 30th CELEBRATION EVENT; and Victini, Zeraora and Alolan Exeggutor from the Chinese Day and Night and Alola Celebration events.

collections.title: Banned Cards
collections.description: Collector shorthand for cards with altered, replaced or controversial artwork. Meet the Japanese originals alongside the international changes and later revisions. These are artwork histories, not a list of cards banned from tournament play; where a motive is unconfirmed, we say so.
collections.coverage: Includes the languages currently in the catalog. Other international languages, Korean and Traditional Chinese are not yet cataloged; this is not a worldwide completeness claim.

description.text: Ken Sugimori's Japanese picture of Misty holding Staryu was replaced for Gym Challenge with a clothed Misty and Squirtle. The original appeared in both the Cerulean City Gym deck and Leaders' Stadium.

Grimer's pupils were moved for Team Rocket so it no longer appeared to look up at the girl above the drain. The artist denied that interpretation of the original. Its Poison Gas effect also changed between the Japanese and English cards.

The Japanese hand pose could be read as a rude gesture. The international card received a different Sugimori illustration. The Japanese picture appeared in both the Saffron City Gym deck and Challenge from the Darkness.

The Japanese expansion picture has a graveyard with tombstones and crosses. The English Gym Heroes card removes that setting. This is the holo Gengar that became English 14/132, not the different illustration on 29/132.

The first Japanese print has an omote manji, a Buddhist symbol far older than Nazism, in the upper left of the picture. Its resemblance to a swastika led to complaints when imported copies reached the United States, and the symbol was replaced with a round emblem in later Japanese print runs and on the English card.
The original Komiya illustration shows Sentret feeding from an udder. The English Neo Genesis card has a different scene, which later Japanese prints adopted too.
The Japanese scene foregrounds the Game Corner's casino-like interior. The international illustration reframes it around the machine itself. The change is documented; a formal ban is not.
Like Arcade Game, this illustration shifts from the Japanese Game Corner setting to a closer view of the game for its international release.
Jynx's face changed from black to purple amid criticism of its original design. Ken Sugimori's painting is black on the Japanese Expansion Pack card and purple on the English Base Set one.
Ken Sugimori's picture from the Japanese Saffron City Gym deck gives Jynx a black face. For Gym Heroes it was colored purple, as on the English Base Set Jynx.
Atsuko Nishida's Jynx from Challenge from the Darkness has a black face too. The English Gym Challenge card colors it purple.

Akira Komayama's Dragon Blade picture points Magmortar's arm cannon at the viewer. Dragons Exalted uses a different pose. The reason for the change has not been confirmed; claims about a weapons policy remain speculation.

collections.title: GB Promos
collections.description: Promotional cards for the Game Boy releases of the Pokémon card games.
collections.coverage: Includes cards with the GB logo: eight Japanese promos and the English Meowth in holo and non-holo.

description.text: The first game was released in Japan as Pokémon Card GB. Dragonite came with the game, Meowth with CoroCoro Comic, and Venusaur with the official guidebook. All three have the GB logo beside the artwork.

sources.title: Elite Fourum · Promo Showcase – Pokemon Card GB Promo

description.text: These five cards all relate to the second game, Pokémon Card GB2: Here Comes Team GR!, which was released only in Japan. Dark Ivysaur and Dark Venusaur came with Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 10, Team GR’s Mewtwo and Lugia with the game, and Dark Fearow with its official guidebook. Their logo still reads GB.

description.text: The holo Meowth came with the English Pokémon Trading Card Game for Game Boy Color. The non-holo version was released in Japan for the JR West Pokémon Stamp Rally 2000. Both have the GB logo in the bottom-right corner of the artwork.
